question.problem: Find the surface area of the portion of the cylinder $z=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ $x=1,$ and the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡x\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14221663/assets/03b9d0f5ae212262bc82e2e2986dfeb6cd3b85f5c8217aba1c7c3c39c97db3d7.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}})=0, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}})=-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(0)^{2}+{(-\frac{y}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+\frac{{y}^{2}}{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{\frac{1}{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\,{|}_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
